title: Recoil transport and environmental exposure of black-hole merger remnants
abstract: Black-hole mergers in stellar clusters leave remnants whose recoil can carry them repeatedly through regions of different stellar density and composition. Their subsequent availability for dynamical interactions depends on the time spent in those environments, as well as on whether they remain bound. We study how gravitational encounters determine finite-time residence and species-resolved exposure. Published multimass distributions for six Galactic clusters provide the adopted potentials and scattering backgrounds. Reconstructions, local anisotropic collision calculations and Galactic environmental controls connect these backgrounds to a merger-conditioned transport formulation. The calculations reveal distinct radial profiles of the black-hole contribution to velocity diffusion. Finite-angle encounter calculations specify a common collision law and separate event frequency from individual deflection strength. We formulate the hypothesis that the accuracy of continuous transport for residence depends on the encounter increments sampled along the orbit and on how those increments change the expected remaining occupation. A matched comparison retains either the full local encounter transitions or their first two velocity-change moments. A backward occupation equation relates their difference in mean residence to a nonlocal generator residual, defining a route from local scattering physics to an observable accuracy criterion. Finite-population response and time-dependent host evolution enter as separate controlled comparisons. Collisionless controls connect these backgrounds to finite-time residence and encounter budgets along equal-energy launches. The matched collisional residence predictions and their response estimate remain to be evaluated.
